analysis:
Reviewed docs/reference/configuration.md head text, lines 945-1433. The only changed range in the supplied patch is line 410: it documents DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK as also skipping the darkbloom cluster pair's update at its slot, via ClusterServiceCommand.supervisorConfiguration. Lines 945-1433 are context and not a changed range, so this is a documentation change only. No code, access control, crypto or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

The documented env var disables only the cluster pair's auto-update, an operator-local opt-out. It is consistent with the existing watchdog and update-skip semantics. It adds no remote or consumer-reachable surface. Operator control over the provider is already within TB-003/ADV-001 scope.

The surrounding context covers cluster runtime facts, model approvals, coordinator-paired members, link fix and isolation. These describe privileged osascript-approved commands built from validated interface names and fixed values, and approval fetch limits (HTTPS only, no redirect, bounded size). I found no contradiction with the threat model there.

Open question for integration: this PR does not show the Swift source for ClusterServiceCommand.supervisorConfiguration. Nothing here verifies that the code honors the documented env behavior. A skipped update could leave a cluster pair on an old or revoked build. That would stay operator-chosen, and the coordinator qualification and revocation controls (T-054) remain authoritative. Cannot confirm from the supplied evidence, but no finding is warranted.
